newsitem.title: UK: Clairvoyant visit fuels speculation on Di and Dodi.
newsitem.headline: Clairvoyant visit fuels speculation on Di and Dodi.

text.p: Britain's tabloid papers were abuzz with speculation that Princess Diana might be about to remarry as news emerged on Wednesday that she had visited a clairvoyant with her new sweetheart, Dodi Fayed.
The top-selling Sun said the couple had flown in a helicopter from London to the northern English home of psychic Rita Rogers, a long-standing confidante of the princess.
The Daily Mail said the helicopter belonged to Harrods, the upmarket London store owned by 41-year-old Dodi's father, Egyptian tycoon Mohamed Al Fayed.
One witness who saw the couple emerge from the psychic's modest home was quoted as saying: "Di was grinning all over her face and looked like she had had good news."
Interest in Diana's love life has leapt with the publication on Sunday of fuzzy pictures that appeared to show her embracing Dodi on a Mediterranean holiday this month.
Tabloids have even begun talking about a winter wedding, a year after Diana's divorce from Prince Charles, the heir to the throne.
Saudi businessman Adnan Khashoggi, Dodi's uncle, did nothing to discourage such talk when he told the London-based Arabic newspaper Asharq al-Awsat: "We welcome Princess Diana into our family."
"Dodi in general is a quiet person and maybe this is what Diana found in him, a good listener," Khashoggi added.
The media were more interested in what Diana and Dodi might have heard from the psychic.
The Sun said Rogers charged 35 pounds ($55) an hour for services which included speaking to clients' dead relatives.
It said Diana had used Rogers to speak to her dead father Earl Spencer, and that she calls the medium from all over the world for advice.
As Diana once again grabbed the limelight, her two teenage sons, Princes William and Harry, were with their father on the royal family's Scottish estate at Balmoral.
In an unusual gesture widely interpreted as an attempt to improve his image, Prince Charles invited photographers to take pictures of himself and his sons on the banks of the River Dee.
